equals under translation

For the stated Boolean conventions, r_B(A)=rc_1(A).

Assumptions & evidence
  • Finite nonempty labeled X and Y
  • A:X x Y->{0,1}
  • Boolean OR-AND factors
  • Unrestricted overlapping all-one rectangle cover
  • k=0 and empty OR are allowed

What the source establishes

Javadi, Maleki and Omoomi supports the factor/rectangle correspondence. It does not separately supply the Atlas empty-support normalization.

How to translate a solution

Forward. For each factor index l, take S_l={x:U[x,l]=1} and T_l={y:V[l,y]=1}. Its support S_l x T_l contains no zero of A, and the union covers every 1-cell; omit empty factors.

Reverse. For each chosen all-one rectangle S_l x T_l, use the indicator of S_l as a factor column and the indicator of T_l as a factor row. Their Boolean OR-AND product reconstructs A.

A factorization with k factors gives a cover with at most k rectangles after empty factors are omitted, while a cover with t rectangles gives a factorization with exactly t factors. The two inequalities make the minima equal.

Atlas convention for the zero case

A is all-zero on the still nonempty X and Y

  • Allow factor dimension k=0
  • Define the empty disjunction as 0
  • Allow the empty rectangle family

The empty Boolean product reconstructs zero and the empty family covers empty support; nonnegative objectives make both minima zero.

r_B(A)=rc_1(A)=0

This boundary case uses the Atlas definitions and argument above.

Keep these meanings separate

  • rc_1 names the covered cell value and maps to S2 kappa(A)
  • It is not S2 kappa_1(A), which restricts each 1-cell to at most one covering rectangle
Ramin Javadi, Zeinab Maleki & Behnaz Omoomi · Introduction, printed p. 2, Boolean-rank/all-one-submatrix correspondence ↗

→
equals under translation

For a graph with its fixed labeled bipartition, rc_1(A_G)=bc(G).

Assumptions & evidence
  • Finite simple bipartite G
  • Fixed labeled nonempty sides X and Y
  • A_G is the X-by-Y biadjacency matrix
  • Bicliques respect the fixed sides

What the source establishes

Javadi, Maleki and Omoomi supports the rectangle/biclique correspondence. The empty-cover normalization is stated separately by the Atlas.

How to translate a solution

Forward. An all-one rectangle S x T gives the biclique with sides S subset X and T subset Y.

Reverse. A covering biclique with sides S subset X and T subset Y gives the all-one rectangle S x T in A_G.

Matrix cells and graph edges correspond one-to-one, preserving cover cardinality in both directions.

Atlas convention for the zero case

G is edgeless on the fixed nonempty sides

  • Allow the empty rectangle family
  • Allow the empty biclique-cover family

Both empty families cover the empty target set; nonnegative cardinalities make both minima zero.

rc_1(A_G)=bc(G)=0

This boundary case uses the Atlas definitions and argument above.

Keep these meanings separate

  • Use the rectangular biadjacency matrix A_G, not the full symmetric adjacency matrix
  • The bipartition is part of the data and may not be changed during translation
Ramin Javadi, Zeinab Maleki & Behnaz Omoomi · Introduction, printed p. 2, rectangle-biclique correspondence ↗

→
exact formula under protocol convention

For nonzero f, N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2 rc_1(M_f)); with the separately defined Atlas zero case, N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2(max(1,rc_1(M_f)))).

Assumptions & evidence
  • Finite nonempty X and Y
  • M_f[x,y]=f(x,y)
  • S2 maximum-leaf-depth nondeterministic protocol convention
  • Accepting-side unrestricted rectangle covers
  • For the cited formula, f has at least one 1-input

What the source establishes

Karchmer, Newman, Saks and Wigderson Proposition 3 and its proof support the nonempty-1-support formula after the explicit notation mapping. The printed logarithm does not resolve rc_1=0.

How to translate a solution

Forward. Given t>=1 covering rectangles, the first party nondeterministically names a row-compatible rectangle using ceil(log_2 t) bits and the second party checks column membership.

Reverse. Accepting leaves of a depth-h binary protocol are all-one rectangles covering every 1-input; there are at most 2^h leaves.

The two inequalities give the ceiling-log equality for nonempty 1-support under the S2 protocol convention.

Atlas convention for the zero case

f is all-zero

  • Set rc_1(M_f)=0 using the empty cover
  • Use a depth-zero constant-reject protocol and set N^1_S2(f)=0

There are no 1-inputs to accept, so constant rejection is sound and complete; depths are nonnegative.

The local totalization equals ceil(log_2(max(1,0)))=0

This boundary case uses the Atlas definitions and argument above.

Keep these meanings separate

  • N^1_S2 is Atlas notation for S2 n(f)
  • It is not S2 n_1(f), which restricts witness multiplicity
  • rc_1 is S2 unrestricted kappa, not kappa_1
  • This is not deterministic communication complexity
  • N^0_S2(f):=N^1_S2(1-f) is an Atlas complement-side definition if later displayed
Mauricio Karchmer, Ilan Newman, Mike Saks & Avi Wigderson · Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pp. 3-5; Proposition 3 and proof ↗

equals under translation

For a graph with its fixed labeled bipartition, lr_B(A_G)=lbc(G).

Assumptions & evidence
  • Same fixed labeled nonempty bipartition as R2
  • Objective is maximum rectangle incidence per row or column
  • Graph objective is maximum biclique incidence per vertex
  • Neither objective is per-cell or per-edge witness multiplicity

What the source establishes

Javadi, Maleki and Omoomi defines the two local-incidence objectives and states their equality. Its text does not separately supply the Atlas empty-cover convention.

How to translate a solution

Forward. Translate every selected rectangle S x T to the corresponding fixed-side biclique. A row or column belongs to exactly the bicliques containing its corresponding graph vertex.

Reverse. Translate each selected fixed-side biclique back to its all-one rectangle; every vertex incidence becomes the corresponding row or column incidence.

Every cover retains the same maximum incidence objective, so the minima agree.

Atlas convention for the zero case

A_G has empty support and G is edgeless on nonempty X and Y

  • Allow empty rectangle and biclique-cover families
  • Assign load zero to every row, column and vertex

The maximum over the still nonempty index or vertex sets is defined and equals zero; nonnegative loads make it minimal.

lr_B(A_G)=lbc(G)=0

This boundary case uses the Atlas definitions and argument above.

Keep these meanings separate

  • Local means maximum participation per row, column or vertex
  • It is not the number of rectangles covering an individual 1-cell and is not S2 bounded witness multiplicity
Ramin Javadi, Zeinab Maleki & Behnaz Omoomi · Introduction, printed pp. 2-3, local Boolean-rank and local biclique-cover paragraphs ↗
